title: valance.web.json
description: Settings for the web target: where the built site is served.

version.description: The version of this file's format.

base.description: The path the site is served under: "/" or "/docs/". Every address the build writes is under it.

url.description: Where the site is published, without a trailing slash. With it, pages get canonical links and the build writes sitemap.xml.

rendering.description: How pages are delivered. "static": every page is rendered to HTML when the site is built and the browser takes it over. "client": no page is written; the host answers every address with the app shell and the browser draws the page (a single route can opt in with delivery: "client"). ("server" is not available yet.)

trailingSlash.description: How a page's address is written: "never" (/guide/a) or "always" (/guide/a/). A page has one address; the page moves the address bar to it when it starts, and links, the sitemap and the canonical link use it.

headers.description: Write the recommended security headers (a strict Content-Security-Policy and others) as _headers beside the built site.

announce.description: After the application changes page in place, tell assistive technology: say the new title in a live region and focus the main content.

base.description: Where its requests go: a path on the site's own origin ("/api") or an absolute https address ("https://api.example.com", which the Content-Security-Policy then allows).

proxy.description: For vlx dev: forward requests under a path "base" to this address ("http://localhost:3000"), so the browser sees one origin and no CORS settings are needed.
